what_it_does: RowHammer is an attack where an adversary hammers a DRAM memory row with rapid repeated reads until neighboring rows suffer bit-flips, corrupting data. The newest DDR5 memory standard includes a built-in defense called Per Row Activation Counting (PRAC), which tracks how many times each row has been accessed and triggers a protective refresh when a threshold is crossed. The problem is that PRAC's counter updates happen in the critical path of every memory read, adding latency, and a clever adversary can mount a 'wave attack' — a precisely timed burst pattern that exhausts the fixed number of refreshes the hardware issues per alarm, effectively defeating the defense. Chronus is a redesigned on-chip DRAM mitigation that moves the counters out of the data array's critical path so they update in parallel rather than adding delay, and it dynamically controls how many refreshes fire per alarm to neutralize wave attacks. The design lives entirely inside the memory chip and has been open-sourced.
